analyst_view.overall: Early view: Brighton (5th, seven points) are the only side in the league phase yet to concede and are second in the Premier League after wins at Manchester City and against Brentford. But Fabian Hurzeler has rotated heavily in Europe (eight changes at Jablonec, five at Getafe) and those sides have scored once in two games. Craiova (8th, seven points) have been solid too, drawing with Getafe and beating Inter Escaldes 3-1 and Egnatia 2-0.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, 2.9 of them for Brighton. I lean lower: Brighton's rotated European sides drew 0-0 at Jablonec and won 1-0 at Getafe, and Hurzeler himself said the competition needs patience against a low block. Craiova have conceded only twice in three games, so a two- or three-goal Brighton win looks more likely than a rout.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, 8.3 for Brighton. Brighton keep the ball for long spells (almost 80% after the break against Brentford, per Sky Sports) and Craiova should sit deep, which supports a high home count. That is already in the number, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, more of them for Craiova. A visiting side defending for long spells tends to pick up tactical fouls on the break, but Brighton's European games have not been feisty and there is no referee yet, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, 22.1 for Brighton. Brighton will have the ball, but at Getafe they were caught on the break: Jaouen Hadjam hit the woodwork twice. That suggests Craiova will get a few chances too, roughly as the number already allows.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, 7.7 for Brighton. I lean lower: at Jablonec Brighton's rotated side kept shooting wide or over, and at Getafe Ibrahim Osman skewed a close-range chance wide, so their European shooting has been loose. Against a Craiova side that has conceded twice in three games, I expect fewer efforts on target than the number.
